item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Good incident and supplement to SCP-668. The response of the foundation seems okay, given that there are a multitude of ways to go about this situation. The cover story should be a story less atrocious than a terrorist attack. This terrorist attack would have made international news, which is more attention then necessary.

There is an unnecessary use of redaction. Redaction used to censor curse words is beneath the Foundation. Unless to keep classified information from leaking, no one cares if the subject said “…motherfucking pigs.” in an incident report about murdering dozens of bystanders.

Other than my notes above, this is very professional and well written.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: There was a pretty easy way to get an air strike onto the target tbh. Just put a locator beacon onto a micro drone, tell an operator to fly it near the target (without telling them about the beacon if necessary), and then tell a pilot who doesn't know about 668 to drop a bomb on the beacon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Man, somehow I only ever remember the entrail wings and go to see if I've upvoted it, and then see that the Foundation's first response to this "in the wild", so to speak, is "NUKE IT FROM SPACE!!"

I'd really like this, except for that. Okay, sure, if it isn't staying in one location, stopping the person holding it would be harder, but defaulting to dropping a nuke? Even overkill like defaulting to telling a tank operator that "the building [the knife is in] is scheduled for a test so please give it all you've got" makes more sense. I can think of a half dozen other ways to do this double blind that do not include the phrase "nuclear detonation", so, despite my desire to upvote this, no vote.

item.title: "I can't shoot him!? Why can't I shoot him!!?"
item.content:encoded:
… this is good.

Question, though: if mines were planted by unknowing Class-D around the mall, the results would have been similar, I suppose. What about a remotely operated drone, whose targeting control and firing control were separated and handled by two different people (the first obviously aware of what they were firing upon, the second unaware).

Also, how does the PsiRI work? I can imagine a mixture of rather esoteric testing along bland and boring IQ, personality and neurology tests.

This is an interesting read! Though it doesn't stand out to me that much, I feel as though the language used is appropriately precise and professional. The level of detail is also really impressive to me.

But, just a minor thing here, "D-061-058 through 070 (12 personnel) were ordered to carry explosive charges to twelve pre-determined points"

…If it's -058 through -070, that's thirteen D-Class, isn't it? So, either the number of personnel or the number of "pre-determined points" should be changed…

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
I basically intended it to work based on information: that is to say, if anyone is aware that they are acting in a hostile manner towards its wielder, it triggers, regardless of range. People with a high psi resistance can avoid it, though.

I think a better call for the final termination would be to cause a group of D-Class Personnel to take a series of actions that would blow up the entire mall: one guy opens up the gas mains, another sets off a spark, that sort of thing.
